# Question

**What percent of young adults in the US move back in with their parents?** Pew Research Center tracked CPS counts of 18–29-year-olds living with parents through the COVID-19 pandemic (Fry, Passel & Cohn, Sept 2020).

## Data source

Published percentages / counts from the Pew report (CPS Feb & Jul 2020); subgroup denominators documented constructions.

# Exploratory analysis

```{python}
#| echo: false
#| fig-cap: "Share of 18–29-year-olds living with parents, July 2020 (dashed: Feb 2020 overall)"
g = df.pivot_table(index=["group", "period"], columns="response",
                   values="count", aggfunc="sum").reset_index()
g["share"] = g["with_parent"] / (g["with_parent"] + g["not_with_parent"])
jul = g[g["period"] == "jul_2020"].sort_values("share")
feb_overall = g[(g["period"] == "feb_2020") &
                (g["group"] == "overall")]["share"].iloc[0]
fig, ax = plt.subplots(figsize=(7.5, 4.2))
ax.barh(jul["group"], jul["share"], color="#4c72b0")
ax.axvline(feb_overall, ls="--", color="#c44e52")
ax.text(feb_overall + 0.005, 0.1, "Feb 2020 overall", color="#c44e52", fontsize=8)
ax.set_xlim(0, 0.85)
ax.set_xlabel("Share living with parents (Jul 2020)")
plt.tight_layout()
plt.show()
```

# Methods & results

One-proportion Wald + bootstrap CIs; two-proportion z for Feb-vs-Jul and demographic contrasts, validated with 100k-replicate randomization.

| Comparison | Result |
|---|---|
| All 18–29 y/o, Jul 2020 | **52.0%** with parents (26.6 M) — record since 1940 |
| vs Feb 2020 (47.0%) | diff +5.0 pp, p < 1e-15 |
| Men vs women (Jul) | 55% vs 49% |
| Ages 18–24 vs 25–29 (Jul) | 71% vs 28% |

# Decision

The pandemic "boomerang" pushed a **majority of young adults back home** for the first time since the Great Depression era; the steep age gradient shows the effect concentrates among the youngest adults.
